title: Almost touching
caption: The Swedish–ESO Submillimetre Telescope under the Milky Way, La Silla Observatory
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The Milky Way stretches across the night sky and seems almost to touch the dish of the Swedish–ESO Submillimetre Telescope, or SEST. The photograph was taken at ESO's La Silla Observatory, 2400 metres up on the outskirts of Chile's Atacama Desert, by A. Ghizzi Panizza.

The band of the Milky Way is shaped by light and darkness. Its bright glow is the light of millions of stars in our galaxy's central region, and the dark patches are clouds of dust that block the light behind them.

SEST was built in 1987 for the Swedish Natural Science Research Council and ESO. This 15-metre radio telescope was, at first light, the only large submillimetre telescope in the southern hemisphere. Over the years it studied everything from comets to stellar nurseries and galaxies. It was decommissioned in 2003, after being overtaken by APEX and ALMA further north in Chile.

understand.summary: This is a night landscape photograph by A. Ghizzi Panizza. The source gives no camera or colour details.
understand.eye: A camera exposure collects far more starlight than the eye, so the Milky Way's bright and dark patches show more strongly than they would to someone standing there.
